name: French Republic

areaKm2.note: world_1938 France polygon = 550,890 km2 computed on the sphere; metropolitan France ~551,500 km2.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1939 = 41,900k (metropolitan France). HYDE/Gapminder (OWID) gives 40.3M; low spans it.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) urban share France 1940 = 53.2%. Low = COW upop/tpop 1939 = 6,397/41,900 = 0.15 (cities over 100,000 only).

activePersonnel.note: Armed forces 5,000,000 after mobilisation (Dear & Foot p. 316, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_France), minus ~0.5M in North Africa, the Levant and other colonies and ~0.15M colonial-recruited soldiers serving in France (excluded, see notes). COW milper 1940 = 5,000k agrees with the total.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: after general mobilisation most trained reservists were already called; remainder = affectes speciaux in war industry and older classes.

supportPersonnel.note: Everything outside the P roles: artillery and tank crews, engineers, signals, train, regional depots and interior, Armee de l'Air (~0.1M) and Marine (~0.16M).

mobilizationRatio.note: Sep 1939: about one-third of men aged 20-45 mobilised, armed forces 5,000,000 (Dear & Foot, Oxford Companion to WWII p. 316) = 0.12 of population. WWI precedent 8.4M mobilised of 39.6M = 0.21 is the ceiling.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Infantry of 117 divisions (104 for the north-east incl. 11 in reserve; Frieser p. 35-37), ~13 of them fortress divisions, plus Maginot sector and regional infantry. 2,240,000 men in army units in the north-east (Dear & Foot / Frieser) include all arms. Reconstruction; grade C.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: MAS 36 only partly issued, many Lebel/Berthier; good FM 24/29 LMG; 25 mm AT gun adequate

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5 (conscripts). Evidence: series B reserve divisions (e.g. 55e and 71e DI at Sedan) poorly trained and aged (Doughty, Breaking Point)

count.note: Chasseurs alpins and pyreneens of the Armee des Alpes and mountain divisions; educated count.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: specialist mountain kit

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: held the Alpine front against Italy in June 1940

count.note: Horse elements of the 5 Divisions Legeres de Cavalerie and 3 spahi/cavalry brigades plus horsed squadrons of the GRDI reconnaissance groups. Educated reconstruction.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: horse cavalry in a mechanised war

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: active cavalry regiments

count.note: French tanks: 3,254 (Frieser p. 36-37) to 3,383-4,071 (Umbreit in GSWW II p. 279; Zaloga 2011 p. 73), via the Battle of France article. Excludes FT-17s in depots.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Char B1 bis and SOMUA S35 out-armoured every German tank; one-man turrets, few radios, short range

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: DCR armoured divisions formed only Jan-May 1940; doctrine of infantry support

count.note: France 10,700 guns in the Allied ~14,000 (Frieser p. 35-37 via Battle of France article); high adds the Alpine front and fortress artillery.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: excellent 75/105/155 mm, much of it WWI vintage, more motorised than German artillery

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: methodical, accurate but slow fire planning

count.note: 764 French fighters with front-line units on 10 May 1940 (Harvey 1990 p. 448, via Battle of France article); Armee de l'Air had 1,562 aircraft in the north-east (Hooton 2007 p. 47) and a reserve of ~2,000 aircraft in depots, mostly unserviceable. High counts depot fighters.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: MS.406 and MB.152 inferior to the Bf 109E; only 36 D.520 delivered by 10 May; Hawk 75 good

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: pilots claimed 2.35:1 air-to-air (Battle of France article, Facon 1996)

count.note: Bombers and reconnaissance: 1,562 front-line aircraft minus 764 fighters = ~800; Germans had about six times as many medium bombers (Harvey p. 448).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: mostly obsolete types; LeO 451 and Breguet 693 arriving in small numbers

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: little ground-support doctrine

count.note: Conway's 1922-1946: 7 battleships (Dunkerque, Strasbourg, 3 Bretagne, Courbet, Paris; Richelieu completing June 1940), carrier Bearn, 7 heavy and ~12 light cruisers.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: modern fast battleships and cruisers; no radar

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional long-service navy

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: very fast large destroyers

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional navy

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: large but mechanically mediocre boats

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: professional crews

count.note: Batteries. Educated guess: French AA was notoriously weak in 1940 (Harvey 1990), mostly 75 mm guns of WWI design and too few 25 mm Hotchkiss.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: obsolescent guns, little fire control

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: reservist crews

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: competent but methodical staff; Gamelin's Dyle-Breda plan left no strategic reserve; slow telephone/courier command (May, Strange Victory; Doughty)

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5 (national conscript army). Evidence: many units fought hard (Gembloux, Stonne, Lille) while some reserve divisions broke at Sedan

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.25-0.5. Evidence: eight months of drole de guerre, political division, memory of 1914-18 losses

weapons.note: Anchor: between 7 (1905) and 8 (1943). Evidence: Char B1 bis 75+47 mm, 25 and 47 mm AT guns; infantry weapons partly WWI

armor.note: Anchor: 8 (rolled homogeneous armour, 1943). Evidence: cast and rolled armour 40-60 mm on S35 and B1 bis, thicker than German tanks of 1940

ships.note: Anchor: between 7 and 8. Evidence: modern fast fleet, a carrier (Bearn, obsolete), no radar

fortification.note: Anchor: 8 (concrete lines: Maginot is the anchor). Evidence: Maginot Line

logistics.note: Anchor: between 7 (railways) and 8 (motor transport). Evidence: about 300,000 army vehicles vs 120,000 German (Frieser p. 29), but rail-based methodical supply

communications.note: Anchor: between 7 (telegraph, telephone) and 8 (radio at company level). Evidence: command relied on telephone and dispatch riders; few tanks had radios

isr.note: Anchor: ISR 7 = aerial recon, 8 = radar. Evidence: aerial reconnaissance spotted the Ardennes columns but warnings were discounted; little radar

air.note: Anchor: air 7 = 1914, 8 = 1943. Evidence: D.520 and Hawk 75 modern but few; most bombers obsolete

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: COW milex 1938 = 919,284 (thousand current US$), 1939 = 1,023,651; against French national income of roughly US$10-12bn this is ~8% in 1938. Grade C (GDP conversion approximate).

industrialShare.note: Analogue: industry ~35% of French output in the late 1930s, agriculture ~25% of output with ~35% of labour. Grade C.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: France was close to self-sufficient in food in 1939, with North African imports.

annualCohort.note: Males reaching 20 in 1939-40 come from the WWI "hollow classes": French births ~0.40M in 1919 and ~0.83M in 1920, halved for males. Educated reconstruction.

armor.note: Educated guess: French tank output reached ~100-150 per month by spring 1940.

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess: deliveries rose sharply in spring 1940 (Hooton 2007 p. 81 reserve of ~2,000 by June); MS.406 1,077 and MB.151/152 636 built in total.

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess: LeO 451, Breguet 691/693 and Amiot 351 in small series.

ships_major.note: Richelieu and Jean Bart completing, La Galissonniere-class cruisers completed 1936-37. Educated per-year rate.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: ~80,000 km routes nationales plus ~250,000 km departmental roads; the much larger network of chemins vicinaux excluded.

railKm.note: SNCF main network ~42,600 km at its 1938 creation; high adds local and secondary lines. Grade C.

majorPorts.note: Marseille, Le Havre, Cherbourg, Brest, Toulon, Bordeaux, Saint-Nazaire, Nantes, Dunkirk, Lorient, Rouen, Calais, La Pallice.

merchantTonnage.note: Lloyd's Register 1939-40: France 1,231 steamers and motorships, 2,933,933 gross tons. Converted to deadweight at x1.5 (x1.3-1.6).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: methodical, rail-based supply doctrine; better motorised than the Germans but organised for positional war.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: ~2.7M horses in France in the late 1930s; the army requisitioned ~0.5M.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar terrain, Maginot Line and fortified cities, population support; no climate depth.

notes: Order of battle = 10 May 1940 (start of the Western campaign); demographic and economic values are 1939. Metropolitan France only: includes is empty, colonial populations are not counted, and the ~150,000 North African and Senegalese soldiers in French divisions in France (DINA, DIC, spahi brigades) are NOT in the P-role counts or activePersonnel; the colonial Army of Africa and Levant (~0.5M) is excluded too. Add them via a colonial snapshot if a scenario needs them. Army and air figures come via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_France as pointer to Frieser (Blitzkrieg Legend, pp. 29, 35-37), Dear & Foot (p. 316), Hooton (2007 p. 47) and Harvey (1990). Sep 1939 differences: 98 divisions mobilised for the Saar offensive with ~2,500 tanks (same article). Navy counts are from Conway's (not fetched, grade B).
